newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil trades lower ahead of New Year.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil trades lower ahead of New Year.

text.p: Singapore oil products were staedy to lower on Tuesday in a dull market ahead of the New Year break with gas oil traded lower on aggressive offers, traders said.

They said a European major sold 30,000 tonnes of gas oil for January 15-19 lifting at $31.95 a barrel, which was below its sale on Monday at $32.50. Traders said the aggressive offers had pressured down the swaps market with January quoted at $32.00/$2.10 down from Monday's $32.15/$32.25.
But they said that China's large demand for the first quarter would support overall sentiment.
Chinese oil industry officials said the country needed to import about one million tonnes of gas oil over the next month to ease domestic shortage.

Jet fuel also slipped with a trader bidding for 100,000 barrels for January 15-19 lifting at $33.50 a barrel, down from a bid on Monday at $33.75 fob, with no sellers emerging. But despite the lower bid, traders said regional demand would continue to support prices. Traders said high freight rates continued to make it difficult to get ships to move products.
Taiwan was to buy by tender 250,000 barrels each of leaded and unleaded 95-octane reformate at around $27 a barrel.

A CPC official said the awards will finalised late Tuesday as it has yet to be approved, he said. The unleaded cargo will be awarded around $27 and the leaded was slightly higher due to high freight costs for leaded cargo. A Dutch trader who did not assess the 92-octane unleaded gasoline grade lower than naphtha prices, emerged to buy a cargo lifting January 16-20 at $25.40 a barrel and later raised it to $25.75, facing no sellers.
Traders said fuel oil prices were likely to stay steady this week on healthy fundamentals as Chinese buying interest emerged while new MidEast exports were absent.
